text.p: Three Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp executives were scheduled for arraignment on Medicare fraud charges Tuesday at 1100 EDT/1500 GMT.
The criminal court hearing was set before U.S. Magistrate George Swartz in U.S. District Court in Fort Myers.

The three to be arraigned are Robert Whiteside, director of reimbursements at Columbia headquarters in Nashville, Tenn.; Michael Neeb, chief financial officer in the firm's northern Florida division; and Jay Jarrell, chief executive in the company's southwest Florida region.

They were charged June 25 in a five-count indictment with conspiring to commit fraud by submitting false cost reports under Medicare and the military's Civilian Health and Medical Program on behalf of Fawcett Memorial Hospital in Port Charlotte, Fla., from 1986 until June.
All three have been free on bond since the indictment was made public on July 30.
If convicted, each faces up to 25 years in prison and fines up to $1.25 million.
Columbia/HCA is the nation's largest for-profit hospital chain and is based in Nashville, Tenn.
It owns 67 Florida hospitals, accounting for one-third of the hospital beds in the state.

Federal investigators are probing its Medicare billing procedures and its incentive plans for doctors. Separately, Florida and other states have launched local probes of its Medicare billing practices.
State pension managers in New York, Florida and Louisiana also have filed civil lawsuits against the company, alleging its managers endangered the value of the stock held in public retirement funds.
Columbia's stock has dipped nearly a third since a federal probe into allegations of Medicare fraud was launched.
